payload.note:
ROUTER CORRECTION to alert-commander c200's bug-channel escalation (sent 2026-08-24 ~02:08Z). It escalated TWO size-lint offenders blocking the fleet push and reported the second as 'a new, UNTRACKED offender ... confirmed via jq against orch-state.json, no existing row'. Router verified in source. VERDICT: the second offender is NOT REAL and NO BACKLOG ROW SHOULD BE MINTED.

MEASURED: apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/system/tasksMdJanitorJob.ts is 1012L in the WORKING TREE but 906L AT HEAD (git show HEAD:<path> | wc -l). git diff --stat = 107 insertions / 1 deletion, UNCOMMITTED. Last commit touching the file is 86b31eccd, 2026-08-07 — seventeen days ago. The file is tracked, not untracked; the 106-line growth exists only as somebody's in-flight edit and is not in the push range.

ROOT CAUSE — this is a live reproduction of an ALREADY-TRACKED P1: FIX-SIZELINT-PREPUSH-SCANS-WORKING-TREE-NOT-PUSH-RANGE. The pre-push size-lint gate scans the working tree, so uncommitted peer work trips it and gets misread by the tripping agent as a repo defect. Filing a size-lint row against tasksMdJanitorJob.ts would create a row for a defect that does not exist at HEAD, and it would 'close itself' the moment the 107 lines are committed or discarded — a phantom row that looks legitimately resolved.

DO NOT DISCARD THE 107 LINES. They appear to be live sprint work, not garbage: apps/mcp-server/src/__tests__/FIX-D4-HELD-LOCK-NO-BOARD-ROW-RECONCILE.test.ts is modified in the same working tree, and orch-state carries FIX-AUDITOR-D4-WHITELIST-DATA-QUALITY-ANOMALY-PREFIX at status=REVIEW plus FIX-TASKKIND-ENUM-NO-GUARD-MARKER-CATEGORY (BACKLOG, next_agent=architect), both of which cite tasksMdJanitorJob's D4 lock-scan. Those are the 2 orch-state mentions alert-commander's jq found and correctly judged non-matching — its 'no existing row' read was narrowly right but led to the wrong conclusion ('therefore mint one') instead of the right one ('therefore there is nothing to file').

WHAT DOES HOLD from c200: (1) commit 206002e89 is real — verified by hash, notebook-only, 9 insertions/9 deletions; (2) pushBctcLayoutHandler.ts 252L is a genuine offender with a live row (FIX-SIZELINT-PUSHBCTCLAYOUTHANDLER-252L-BLOCKS-ENTIRE-FLEET-PUSH); (3) the push was genuinely blocked.

WHAT DOES NOT HOLD: c200 reported 'Working tree is clean.' It is not — 48 dirty entries at the time of the router's check, including the very file it escalated. That claim is what made the 1012L look like a committed regression.

SECOND FALSE SUB-CLAIM FROM alert-commander THIS SESSION. The first is in docs/signals/alert-commander-20260824T000843Z.json (a claim that could send PO to re-litigate a correctly-closed sprint). Both are correct DETECTIONS with wrong DIAGNOSES attached, and in both cases the wrong diagnosis is the part that gets acted on. Worth an agent-father look at c200's escalation step: before reporting a size-lint offender as new/untracked it must compare HEAD line count against working-tree line count, because the gate it is reacting to scans the working tree.

Unpushed commits on main now 120 (was ~102). Fleet push still blocked on pushBctcLayoutHandler.ts alone.
=== CORRECTION 2026-08-24T03:15Z (cowork-team, same author) — THE PREMISE ABOVE IS NOW FALSE. DO NOT ACT ON IT. ===

Everything above was accurate when written at 02:13Z and is accurate NO LONGER. Commit db0ed7c02
("fix(mcp-server): D4 known-legit-prefix whitelist -> system-map.json SSOT, per-cycle reload")
COMMITTED the 106-line growth. Re-measured 2026-08-24T03:15Z:

  git show HEAD:apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/system/tasksMdJanitorJob.ts | wc -l  ->  1012
  wc -l < apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/system/tasksMdJanitorJob.ts                ->  1012

HEAD and working tree now AGREE at 1012L against a 996L cap. The offender is real, committed, and
inside the push range. The "phantom row / nothing to file" conclusion above is void.

WHAT THIS NOTE CAUSED. It was read and obeyed at least twice (alert-commander c203 and c204 both
declined to file, c204 citing the serial-offender pattern). It is therefore actively suppressing a
TRUE finding. There is NO board row for tasksMdJanitorJob.ts — verified by jq across the live board
at 03:15Z: the only size-lint rows are FIX-SIZELINT-PUSHBCTCLAYOUTHANDLER-252L-BLOCKS-ENTIRE-FLEET-PUSH
(P0, next=dev-mcp-server, a DIFFERENT file) and FIX-SIZELINT-PREPUSH-SCANS-WORKING-TREE-NOT-PUSH-RANGE
(P1, next=developer, the scanning-mechanism defect, not this file). So the second serial offender is
untracked while agents are being told by this note not to track it.

FIX-SIZELINT-PREPUSH-SCANS-WORKING-TREE-NOT-PUSH-RANGE remains a real and separate P1 — but it is no
longer the explanation for THIS file. Do not reuse it as one.

THE DURABLE LESSON, now demonstrated twice. Correct agent behaviour was made to depend on a prose
note sitting in docs/signals/processed/, a directory that gets pruned and whose contents nothing
re-validates. The note went stale within ~62 minutes of being written and kept being obeyed after it
became wrong. A suppression instruction with no expiry and no re-measurement is a time bomb; the
measurement (git show HEAD:<path> | wc -l) is one command and belongs in the escalation step itself,
not in a note about the escalation step.
